agentSummary:
I built the dashboard as a 3-page app called "Pulse Analytics": Overview, Customers and Settings, all running on in-memory sample data. `npm run build` passes and `npm run lint` is clean. I haven't opened it in a browser, so the mobile layout, charts and interactions haven't been checked visually; that's the main thing left to confirm.

**Setup.** The project had no Tailwind, which Nucleux needs, so I installed `tailwindcss@3`, `postcss` and `autoprefixer` as dev dependencies and added the Nucleux preset config. I also made `recharts@2.15.4` and `lucide-react@0.469.0` direct dependencies; they were already in `node_modules` as dependencies of Nucleux, at those same versions. `@nucleux/react` and `@nucleux/tokens` were not changed.

**Layout (all pages)**
- On large screens there's a left navigation column; below that width it becomes a menu button that opens the same links in a slide-out panel.
- The top bar has customer search on screens 640px and up (Enter jumps to the Customers page with the search filled in), a notifications button and the user's avatar.
- Navigation uses simple URL hash links (`#/customers`), since the project has no router.

**Overview**
- Four KPI cards: monthly recurring revenue, active customers, revenue churn and average revenue per account. Each shows the change from last month with an arrow, the percentage and colour, so the trend doesn't rely on colour alone.
- A range picker (6 or 12 months) controls two charts: a revenue trend and monthly active users split by plan. Both use Nucleux theme colours and include a text summary for screen readers.
- A "revenue by plan" panel with progress bars, and a recent sign-ups table that hides less important columns on small screens.

**Customers**
- Search by company, contact or email, plus plan and status filters and a "Clear filters" button. A count shows how many of the 42 customers match.
- The table sorts and pages through results (10 per page). On phones it drops to customer and status columns, adds plan and revenue from 640px, and seats and sign-up date from 1024px.
- "View" on a row opens a side panel with the customer's details. "Export CSV" downloads whatever rows are currently filtered.

**Settings** (four tabs)
- **Profile:** a form that checks required fields and email format, saves explicitly and shows a confirmation.
- **Notifications:** five on/off switches that apply immediately with a short confirmation pop-up.
- **Billing:** current plan, seats used and an invoices table.
- **Security:** a two-factor switch, "sign out other sessions", and a "Delete workspace" button that asks for confirmation. It's demo only, so nothing is deleted.

**Loading and error states.** Each page shows a short simulated load with placeholder blocks first. Adding `?fail` to the URL makes the loads fail so you can see the error message and Retry button.

**Things to know**
- The sample user is "Alex Morgan" at `alex@pulse.example`. I deliberately didn't use your name or email in the sample data.
- The "Active customers" and "Avg. revenue per account" month-on-month changes are fixed sample figures, not calculated, because the sample data has no customer history.
- `src/App.css` is left over from the template and no longer used. My delete command was blocked, so you can remove it.
- The build warns that the main JavaScript file is over 500 kB, mostly because of the charting library. It's only a warning; splitting each page into its own file would fix it.
- Nucleux had everything this needed. Small app-specific pieces (KPI card, status badge, settings row) are made from Nucleux parts, with no hand-built replacements for library components.

The main code is in `src/components/AppShell.tsx`, `src/pages/` (one file per page) and `src/data.ts` (sample data).

I built the storefront, and `npm run build` passes (`tsc -b` plus `vite build`). `npm run lint` is also clean. I couldn't look at it in a browser, though: the permission mode blocked starting the dev server and a headless browser. So the layout at 360px wide is checked only by reading the code. Open it with `npm run dev` before relying on the phone layout.

## Setup
The project had no Tailwind, which Nucleux needs, so I added Tailwind v3, autoprefixer and lucide-react (for icons) as dependencies. I set up the Nucleux Tailwind preset and imported its theme CSS in `src/main.tsx`. `@nucleux/react` and `@nucleux/tokens` were not reinstalled and their versions are unchanged. `src/App.css` is no longer used, but I couldn't delete it (file removal was blocked), so it's still there.

## What you can do in it
Navigation uses URL `#` routes, since the project has no router package.

- **Shop (`#/`)**: a grid of 12 sample products in 5 categories. You can filter by category, search by text and sort by price or rating.
  - The grid is 1 column on phones and up to 4 on wide screens.
  - A short simulated load shows placeholder cards first. There is also a load-error state with Retry, and an empty state with "Clear filters".
  - Each card has a quick "Add" button and shows "Sale", "New", "Only N left" or "Sold out" labels as text.
- **Product page (`#/product/:id`)**: breadcrumb, price, colour choice, quantity control capped by stock, and an Add to cart button. Below that are Details and Shipping & returns tabs and related products. Loading and not-found states are handled.
- **Cart**: a cart drawer opens from the header icon, which shows the item count, and there is a full cart page.
  - You can change quantities, remove items, or clear the cart after a confirmation dialog.
  - The order summary shows subtotal, shipping (free over $100), 8% tax and total.
- **Checkout (`#/checkout`)**: three steps (shipping, then delivery and payment, then review). Each step is checked before you can move on.
  - Errors appear next to each field, with a summary at the top, and focus jumps to the first bad field.
  - It checks email format, 5-digit ZIP, card number validity, expiry not in the past, and security code length (4 digits for Amex).
  - The review step lets you jump back to edit any section and needs the terms box ticked.
  - Card number `4000 0000 0000 0002` simulates a decline so you can see the payment-failure message. `4242 4242 4242 4242` goes through.
- **Order confirmation (`#/order/:id`)**: the placed order is kept in memory only, so reloading this page shows "Order not found".

## How it follows Nucleux
Each page starts from a Nucleux pattern: product list for the shop, record detail for the product page, multi-step form for checkout, and the loading/empty/error states pattern everywhere. I checked the planned components and props with the Nucleux validator. Styling uses Nucleux colour and spacing names only, with no hard-coded colours.

## Where I departed from Nucleux, and why
- **Product grid instead of a table**: the list pattern calls for a data table, but its own guidance says to use cards for visual items, so products are cards.
- **No side navigation**: a shop has no sections to switch between, so I used just a sticky top bar. On phones the header search hides and an in-page search takes its place.
- **Built from Nucleux pieces because Nucleux doesn't ship them**:
  - **Quantity stepper:** Nucleux has none.
  - **Cart count bubble:** Nucleux has none.
  - **Product images:** the sample data has no photos, so each category gets a coloured tile with an icon.
- **Colour and delivery options**: Nucleux's radio buttons can't be moved between with the arrow keys, only with Tab.

I built the room-booking app with Nucleux components throughout, and `npm run build` and `npm run lint` both pass. I haven't opened it in a browser, so the layout at phone width (360px) hasn't been checked by eye. It was built following the Nucleux responsive rules, but it hasn't been looked at.

**What it does** (`npm run dev`)
- **Book a room** (`#/rooms`): a page header, a search box, filters for room type and group size, and a grid of 7 sample rooms. Each card shows the room's type, capacity, floor and amenities, with a "Check availability" button. One column on phones, two from tablet width, three on wide screens.
- **Room page** (`#/rooms/:id`):
  1. **Pick a date:** a calendar that allows today up to 60 days ahead; Sundays and past days can't be picked.
  2. **Pick a time:** choose 1–4 hours, then a start time between 8 AM and 6 PM. Times already taken by you, by other members (simulated) or already past are disabled and crossed out.
  3. **Your booking:** a summary panel with one main "Review and confirm" button. It sits beside the steps on large screens and below them on phones.
  4. **Confirm dialog:** recaps the booking and asks for a booking name, number of attendees (checked against the room's capacity) and optional notes. If the slot was taken in the meantime, the dialog stays open with an error. On success you get a confirmation message and land on My bookings.
- **My bookings** (`#/bookings`): Upcoming and Past/cancelled tabs, with the upcoming count in the tab label and the side navigation. Each booking shows date, time, room, attendees and status ("Confirmed", "Completed", "Cancelled" as text, not just colour). Cancel asks first, naming the booking and what happens ("Keep booking" / "Cancel booking"), then shows a confirmation message.
- **Loading and empty states:** every list shows placeholder shapes while loading, a message when empty, and an error with Retry. Add `?simulateError` to the URL to see the error state.

**How it's put together**
- Bookings live in memory in `src/store.tsx` with a short fake delay; refreshing the page resets them to the sample data. Rooms and helpers are in `src/data.ts`.
- Navigation is a small hash-based router (`src/router.ts`), since the project had no router.
- Nucleux has no page layout for picking a time slot, so I built that step from Nucleux's toggle buttons inside a card.

**Changes outside the app code**
- **Tailwind added:** `tailwindcss@3`, `postcss` and `autoprefixer` are new dev dependencies, with `tailwind.config.js` and `postcss.config.js`. Nucleux's setup requires them and they weren't installed. The `@nucleux` packages were left as they were.
- **Icons added:** `lucide-react@0.469.0` is now a direct dependency, at the same version Nucleux already pulled in.
- **Leftover file:** `src/App.css` from the Vite template is unused, but I couldn't delete it because the command was blocked. It's safe to remove.

## Pages

Every page sits inside one shared app shell built on the Nucleux `app-shell` pattern. On wide screens the navigation is a left panel; below the `lg` breakpoint (1024px) a menu button opens the same links in a slide-out drawer.

| Route | What it does | Main Nucleux components |
|---|---|---|
| `#/users` | Users table: search by name, email or team; filter by role and status; "Clear filters"; a live result count; sortable columns; 10 rows per page. The "Invite user" button is the page's one primary action. Filters are kept when you go to a user and come back. | PageHeader, SearchInput, Select, DataTable, Badge, Avatar, ErrorState, Skeleton |
| Invite user dialog | Email (checked for format and for people already in the workspace), name, role and team, and an optional message. The send button is disabled while sending; a toast confirms. Owner can't be granted by invite. | Dialog, Label, Input, Select, Textarea, Button, toast |

Suspend, Remove and Reset MFA each ask for confirmation, naming the user and the consequence. | Breadcrumb, PageHeader, Tabs, cards, ActivityLog, AlertDialog |

## Behaviour
- **Data:** about 42 sample users and 120 audit events, generated the same way on every load. Every change you make in the UI (invite, role change, suspend, reactivate, remove, MFA reset, resend invite) is written to the audit log in memory, attributed to the signed-in admin.
- **Loading, empty and error states:** every data view has them. Loading is simulated with a 600ms delay. Add `?fail=1` to the URL to see the error state; Retry then succeeds.
- **Small screens:** less important table columns (Team, Last active, Details, IP) are hidden on narrow screens rather than squeezed, and toolbars stack vertically.
- **Accessibility:** every control has a label, status is shown as text and not only colour, error messages are announced, and the page title changes with the route.

## Setup changes
- Added Tailwind v3, PostCSS and autoprefixer as dev dependencies, with `tailwind.config.js` and `postcss.config.js` per the Nucleux setup guide. Tailwind is required for Nucleux components to be styled.
- Added `lucide-react` (icons) as a direct dependency.
- Replaced the starter CSS in `src/index.css` and imported `@nucleux/tokens/styles.css` in `main.tsx`.
- The `@nucleux/react` and `@nucleux/tokens` versions are unchanged.

## What I built myself, and why
- **Routing:** a small hash router in `src/lib/router.ts`, because the project has no router and this keeps dependencies down.
- **Helpers:** a media-query hook and a hook that saves filters for the browser tab. Nucleux has no hooks for these.
- **Role permissions are fixed:** you change which role a user has, but you can't create or edit roles.
- **No per-row menu:** Nucleux's Menu is only a panel with no trigger or popover, so instead of a per-row actions menu, the user's name links to their detail page.
- **Unused file:** the starter `src/App.css` is still there. Nothing imports it; I couldn't delete it because shell deletes weren't permitted here.

## Nucleux usage
The layout and components come from Nucleux's own page patterns. The design checker reported no errors; its 4 warnings were normal HTML attributes like `href` and `htmlFor`. The pieces I wrote myself are all built from Nucleux parts:
- **`MemberCard`:** Nucleux has no person card, so I composed one from its card, avatar and badge components.
- **The member avatar stack** in the teams table.
- **A small screen-size hook** used to hide table columns on phones.

Two notes:
- **No dropdown menus:** Nucleux's menu component has no button to open it, so table row actions are plain buttons instead.
- **Team form is a full page, not a dialog:** Nucleux has no pattern for a full-page form. The member checklist makes the form too long for a dialog, so I followed the settings-page layout.

Code is in `src/` (`pages/`, `components/`, `data/`, `router.ts`).

**Setup.** Nucleux needs Tailwind v3, which the project didn't have. I added `tailwindcss@3`, `postcss`, `autoprefixer` and `lucide-react` (for icons), plus the config files and the Nucleux theme import in `main.tsx`. I didn't touch the `@nucleux/*` packages or their versions.

**Layout.** I followed Nucleux's app-shell pattern: a side navigation on wide screens, a menu button that opens a slide-in drawer below that, and a top bar with search and your avatar. The avatar updates when you save your profile. Overview, Projects and Team are just placeholders that link back to Settings. The settings page itself follows Nucleux's settings-page pattern: four tabs, each linked to its own URL (`#/settings/profile`, `/notifications`, `/security`, `/billing`). While data loads you see placeholder skeletons, and if loading fails you get an error message with a Try again button.

**The four tabs:**
- **Profile:** name, username, email, job title, bio (with a 0/160 counter), website, time zone and language, plus photo upload (images only, up to 2 MB). Errors show once you leave a field or press Save. Save and Discard only turn on when something has changed. If saving fails, your input is kept and the reason is shown on the field and in a red banner; try the username `admin`, which the fake server treats as taken.
- **Notifications:** on/off switches for email and push across five topics, plus a daily/weekly/never digest choice. These take effect immediately with a short confirmation pop-up, so there's no Save button. Security alerts are always on.
- **Security:**
  - **Password change:** current, new and confirm fields with show/hide buttons, a strength bar, and a requirements checklist marked with icons and text, not just colour. A wrong current password is rejected; the demo password is shown on screen (`Sample-pass-2026`).
  - **Two-factor:** an on/off switch.
  - **Active sessions:** a table where you can sign out one device or all others, each behind a confirmation dialog. It shows an empty message when only this device is left.
- **Billing:**
  - **Current plan:** your plan, the next charge, and seat and storage usage bars.
  - **Plan change:** choose monthly or yearly and Free, Pro or Business, then review and confirm in a dialog. Plans with fewer seats than you use are disabled with the reason shown.
  - **Card update:** a dialog that checks the card number, expiry date and security code.
  - **Invoices:** a table with download buttons, which only show a pop-up since there are no real files.
  - **Cancel:** cancelling and resuming the subscription, with a confirmation step.

**Sample data.** Everything lives in memory in `src/data/`, with a short fake delay so the loading and saving states actually appear. Adding `?simulateError` to the URL makes the first load fail so you can see the error screen and retry.

**Where I departed from Nucleux:**
- The Nucleux pattern disables Save while the form is invalid. I left it on whenever there are changes, so pressing it reveals every error at once.
- Four tabs are a tight fit at 360px wide, so the tab bar scrolls sideways on very narrow screens.
- Nucleux has no ready-made component for a settings row or a labelled form field, so I built small ones (`SettingRow`, `FormField`) from Nucleux parts and colour tokens. Everything else is standard Nucleux components.

**Leftovers.** I wasn't allowed to delete files, so the unused `src/App.css` and `src/assets/react.svg` from the template are still there; nothing imports them and they're safe to remove.

## What's in it

**App frame:** a left navigation column with Shipments and Exceptions on large screens. Below 1024px it becomes a menu button that opens the same links in a slide-in drawer. The top bar has a dark/light toggle and a "Demo" dropdown for switching between live data, a slow network, a server error and no data, so you can see each state.

**Sample data:** 240 generated shipments that come out the same every run. Each has 15 fields: ID, tracking number, customer, contact, route, carrier, mode, status, priority, pickup date, ETA, weight, pieces, cost and a tracking history. The fake data layer adds a short delay, can fail on demand, and supports cancelling a shipment.

**Shipments list:**
- Four summary cards: in transit, delivered, delayed and exceptions.
- Search by ID, tracking number, customer, city or carrier, plus filters for status, mode, carrier and priority, a "Clear filters" button and a live "Showing X of Y" count.
- Up to 13 columns, sortable by clicking the headers. Status and priority sort in a logical order rather than alphabetically.
- Pagination with a 10/25/50 rows-per-page choice.
- Columns adapt to screen width: on phones the table keeps ID, status and ETA, and folds the customer and route into the ID cell. Customer and route come back from 640px, carrier/mode/priority/pickup from 1024px, and weight/pieces/cost/last update from 1280px. Wide tables scroll inside their own box.
- Overdue ETAs are flagged in text, and statuses show an icon plus a label so they don't rely on colour.
- An "Export CSV" button downloads the filtered rows.
- Filters are kept when you open a shipment and come back.
- **Exceptions** is the same page limited to delayed, exception and overdue shipments.

**Shipment detail:** a breadcrumb back to the list, a header with status and priority, and two actions: "Copy tracking #" and "Cancel shipment". Cancelling asks for confirmation in a dialog that names the shipment, then shows a notification and updates the list. There are two tabs: an Overview with the shipment details, a route-progress bar and the latest update, and a Tracking tab with the full event history.

**Loading, empty and error states:** both views show placeholder skeletons shaped like the content while loading, and an error message with a Retry button on failure. The list distinguishes "no shipments at all", "no open exceptions" and "no filter matches" (which offers Clear filters). The detail page shows a "Shipment not found" state with a way back to the list.

Every page follows Nucleux's own patterns for the app frame, list page, detail page and page states, and only Nucleux components are used. Before writing code I checked the plan with Nucleux's design validator.

## Limitations of the Nucleux table
- **Sort and page reset:** sorting and the current page are held inside the table. Changing rows-per-page re-creates the table, which resets both, and the current page isn't kept when you return from a detail view.
- **Screen readers:** sortable headers don't tell screen readers which way they are sorted.
- **Row clicks:** whole rows can't be clicked, so the shipment ID is the link to the detail view.

agentSummary:
I built the project management app ("Acme Projects"). `npm run build` passes and `npm run lint` is clean. I haven't opened it in a browser, so the layouts at different screen widths (down to 360px) and dark mode follow the Nucleux pattern rules but haven't been checked by eye.

## Setup changes
- **Tailwind:** Nucleux needs Tailwind v3, which wasn't installed. I added `tailwindcss@3`, `postcss` and `autoprefixer` as dev dependencies, plus `tailwind.config.js` and `postcss.config.js` as Nucleux's setup guide specifies.
- **Icons and charts:** `lucide-react@0.469.0` and `recharts@2.15.4` were already installed as sub-dependencies. I listed them in `package.json` at those same versions.
- **Nucleux:** `@nucleux/react` and `@nucleux/tokens` were not reinstalled and their versions are unchanged.
- **Leftover file:** I wasn't allowed to delete `src/App.css`. Nothing imports it, so you can remove it.

## Pages
| Route | Built from Nucleux pattern | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| Frame around every page | `app-shell` | Left menu on large screens; a menu button opens it as a slide-out drawer on small screens. Top bar has task search, a notifications popover and an account link |
| `#/` Dashboard | `dashboard-overview` | 4 headline numbers, project progress bars, "My open tasks", recent activity table |
| `#/projects` | `list-page` | Search, status filter, sortable table with progress bars, "New project" form |
| `#/projects/:id` | `dashboard-overview` + task board | Breadcrumb, summary cards (progress, timeline, team), that project's tasks, edit and delete with confirmation |
| `#/tasks` | `list-page` | Board view (4 status columns) or list view (sortable table with done checkboxes). Filters for project, assignee and priority. Create, edit, move between columns and delete. Toast messages confirm each change |
| `#/analytics` | `dashboard-overview` + charts | Completion rate, cycle time, on-time rate and overdue count. Charts for weekly throughput, open work by priority, status by project and team workload. Can be narrowed to one project |
| `#/team` | `list-page` | Members table with role changes, invite form with validation, remove with confirmation |
| `#/settings` | `settings-page` | Tabs for Profile, Notifications, Appearance (light/dark/system) and Workspace |

## How it works
- **Data:** everything is sample data held in memory (`src/data.ts`, `src/store.tsx`). Loading is faked with a 700ms delay, so every page shows its loading skeleton first. Changes are lost on page reload.
- **Testing error states:** Settings → Workspace has a "Simulate load failure" switch. Turn it on, reload, and you'll see the error message with a Retry button.
- **Routing:** I wrote a small hash-based router (`src/router.ts`) instead of adding a router library.
- **Styling:** colours, including chart series, come only from Nucleux design tokens. There are no hard-coded colour values.
- **Accessibility:** every form control has a label and icon-only buttons have names. Status always appears as text in a badge, never by colour alone. Charts have text descriptions for screen readers.

## Gaps in Nucleux
- **No task card or board.** I built `TaskCard` and the board columns from Nucleux's Card, Badge, Avatar, Popover and Menu components.
- **No menu-button component.** Menus open from a popover trigger styled to match the other icon buttons.
- **No router.** Hence the small custom one above.

## Open issues
- **Bundle size:** the build warns that the JavaScript bundle is 842 kB (234 kB compressed), mostly the chart library. Loading the Analytics page only when it's opened would fix it; I didn't do that.
- **Settings that don't do anything yet:** time zone, "week starts on" and "Compact board cards" can be changed but have no effect. The notification switches and the workspace name don't change anything beyond the page itself.
